memory_candidates.content: check-extension-docs.sh's check_deployed_script_drift() (Rule F) treats a manifest-declared script with an ABSENT deployed copy as an intentional 'not deployed' info line, never a FAIL -- it only FAILs on content mismatch when BOTH the deployed and extension-source copies exist. This lets an extension manifest declare a superset of scripts (some deployed/live, some source-only/deferred) without tripping the drift guard, as long as truly-deployed copies stay byte-identical to source.

Before trusting a research report's claim that a file is 'never deployed' or 'source-only', re-verify against the live filesystem at implementation time -- research and implementation can be separated by unrelated commits from other tasks that change deployment state (e.g. task 763 deployed test-lit-pipeline.sh independently of the zotero/cite research in task 844, making an earlier finding stale).
